t: Which of the following is NOT a liability insurance policy?
e: A fire floater insures the insured's own stocks against fire — a first-party property cover; the other three indemnify legal liability to others.

topic: Law of Torts and Legal Liability
t: To succeed in an action for negligence, the plaintiff must establish:
o: Only that the defendant owed a duty of care
A duty of care, its breach, and resulting damage
That the defendant intended to cause harm
e: All three elements are necessary; intention is not required, as negligence is a failure to take reasonable care.

t: The maximum Any One Accident (AOA) limit available under the Public Liability Insurance Act policy is:
e: The AOA limit equals the owner's paid-up capital subject to a maximum of ₹5 crore, with the AOY limit at three times the AOA (maximum ₹15 crore).

topic: Employers' Liability and Employees' Compensation Insurance
t: The minimum compensation payable for death of an employee under the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923 (as amended in 2009) is:
e: Death compensation is 50% of wages × relevant factor or ₹1,20,000, whichever is more; the corresponding minimum for permanent total disablement is ₹1,40,000.

t: D&O liability policies are generally written on:
e: Claims-made wording lets the insurer close its exposure at expiry; the policy covers claims first made during the period for wrongful acts after the retroactive/continuity date.

topic: Cyber and Other Specialised Liability Covers
t: 'Cyber extortion' cover under a cyber policy indemnifies:
o: Ransom payments and negotiation costs arising from a ransomware or extortion threat
Liability to customers for data loss
e: Extortion cover is a first-party section responding to credible threats to damage systems or release data unless payment is made.

topic: Underwriting and Claims in Liability Insurance
t: Where two liability policies cover the same claim, the principle of contribution requires that:
o: The policy issued first pays the whole claim
The insured chooses which policy pays
The insurers share the loss rateably between them
e: Contribution prevents the insured recovering twice; most liability policies contain a non-contribution or 'other insurance' clause to regulate the sharing.

t: A quota share treaty is one where:
o: Losses above a retention are paid by the reinsurer
The cedant cedes a fixed percentage of every risk and premium within the treaty
The annual loss ratio is protected
Losses from one event across policies are protected
e: Quota share is proportional: premium and losses are shared in the same fixed ratio, and the reinsurer pays a commission.

topic: Law of Torts and Legal Liability
t: Defences available to a defendant under the strict liability rule of Rylands v Fletcher include:
o: Act of God, act of a stranger, default of the plaintiff, statutory authority and consent of the plaintiff
Only proof of absence of negligence
e: These exceptions distinguish strict liability from the absolute liability of M.C. Mehta, under which no exceptions are allowed.

t: Under Section 3 of the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991, a claimant seeking relief is NOT required to prove:
o: Any wrongful act, neglect or default of the owner
That a hazardous substance was being handled
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 3 imposes no-fault liability on the owner; the claimant must only establish the accident involving the hazardous substance and the resulting injury or damage.

t: Under the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991, 'owner' means:
o: Only the occupier of a factory
Only the manufacturer of the hazardous substance
Only the transporter of the hazardous substance
A person who owns, or has control over handling, any hazardous substance at the time of the accident
e: The definition is wide and includes firms, associations and any person in control of handling the substance, so that liability attaches to whoever is in charge.

t: An industrial public liability policy has an AOA limit of ₹1 crore and a compulsory excess of ₹50,000 per accident. A third-party claim is settled for ₹8 lakh. The insurer pays:
e: The excess is deducted from the claim: ₹8,00,000 − ₹50,000 = ₹7,50,000, well within the AOA limit.

t: A claims-made products liability policy for 2025-26 has a retroactive date of 1 April 2022. A product sold in 2021 injures a user in June 2025 and the claim is made in August 2025. The claim is:
o: Not covered because the product was sold before the retroactive date
Not covered because the policy is on an occurrence basis
Covered, because the injury occurred after the retroactive date and the claim was made during the policy period
Covered only if the product was sold within the policy period
e: The retroactive date relates to when the injury/damage occurs, not when the product was sold; both conditions of the claims-made trigger are satisfied.

t: Standard exclusions in a professional indemnity policy include:
o: Fines, penalties, punitive damages and deliberate dishonest acts
e: Negligence, errors and omissions are the very subject of PI cover; penalties and intentional wrongdoing are uninsurable or against public policy.

topic: Employers' Liability and Employees' Compensation Insurance
t: If an employer fails to pay compensation under the Employees' Compensation Act within one month of it falling due, the Commissioner may direct payment of simple interest at:
e: Section 4A provides for 12% simple interest and, if there is no justification for the delay, an additional penalty of up to 50% of the compensation.

t: A 'wrongful act' under a D&O policy is generally defined as:
o: Any actual or alleged breach of duty, neglect, error, misstatement, misleading statement or omission by a director or officer in that capacity
Only an act causing bodily injury
e: The wide definition includes allegations, so that defence costs are triggered even when the claim is ultimately unfounded.

t: A CGL policy has an each-occurrence limit of ₹2 crore and a general aggregate of ₹5 crore. Three covered occurrences in the year produce losses of ₹2.5 crore, ₹1.5 crore and ₹1.8 crore. The insurer pays in total:
e: First loss limited to ₹2 cr, second ₹1.5 cr (total ₹3.5 cr), third limited by the remaining aggregate of ₹1.5 cr, giving ₹5 crore in all.

topic: Cyber and Other Specialised Liability Covers
t: Which provision of the Information Technology Act, 2000 makes a body corporate liable to pay compensation for negligence in implementing reasonable security practices for sensitive personal data?
e: Section 43A (inserted in 2008) created civil liability for data breaches, a key statutory basis for cyber liability claims in India.

topic: Cyber and Other Specialised Liability Covers
t: A lift (third party) liability policy covers:
o: Injury to the lift operator employed by the insured
Third-party bodily injury or property damage arising from the use of passenger lifts in the insured's building
e: The policy is a specialised public liability cover for lift owners; breakdown is covered by a machinery policy and the operator by an EC policy.

t: The percentage of obligatory cession to GIC Re applicable to Indian general insurers since financial year 2022-23 is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). IRDAI reduced the obligatory cession from 5% to 4% with effect from 1 April 2022, and this level has continued for subsequent years.

topic: Underwriting and Claims in Liability Insurance
t: Which of the following statements about an 'occurrence' basis liability policy is INCORRECT?
o: It covers injury or damage occurring during the policy period regardless of when the claim is made
It creates a long tail of claims for the insurer
It is generally preferred by insureds
The claim must be made during the policy period
e: The occurrence trigger is the happening of the injury/damage; the claim may come years later, which is the defining feature of this basis.

t: An excess of loss layer is written as '₹4 crore excess of ₹1 crore'. On a loss of ₹3.5 crore the reinsurer pays:
e: The cedant retains the first ₹1 crore; the reinsurer pays the excess up to ₹4 crore, i.e. ₹3.5 cr − ₹1 cr = ₹2.5 crore.

t: Public liability and other liability rates in India were freed from tariff control with effect from:
e: IRDAI detariffed general insurance (other than motor TP) from 1 January 2007, allowing insurers to rate liability risks on their own experience.

topic: Law of Torts and Legal Liability
t: The distinction between libel and slander is that:
o: Libel is spoken and slander is written
There is no distinction in law
Libel is defamation in a permanent form (e.g. written), while slander is transient (e.g. spoken)
e: Both are forms of defamation covered under 'personal injury' sections of liability policies, but libel is generally actionable without proof of special damage.

t: Under Section 164 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended in 2019), the no-fault compensation payable for death in a motor accident is:
e: The 2019 amendment fixed no-fault compensation at ₹5 lakh for death and ₹2.5 lakh for grievous hurt, replacing the old Section 140 amounts.

t: Section 197(13) of the Companies Act, 2013 provides that the premium paid by a company for D&O insurance:
o: Is not treated as part of the director's remuneration unless the director is proved guilty of the misconduct insured against
Cannot be paid by the company at all
Is always treated as managerial remuneration
Can be paid only for independent directors
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The section expressly allows companies to insure KMP against negligence, default, breach of duty etc.; the premium becomes remuneration only if the person is proved guilty.

t: The default territorial limit of a standard Indian public liability policy is:
e: Cover applies to accidents occurring in India with Indian jurisdiction; wider territorial limits can be granted by endorsement at additional premium.

t: Liability arising from products that are incorporated into aircraft is, under a standard products liability policy:
o: Excluded, given the catastrophic exposure of aviation products
Covered subject to a higher excess
e: Aviation products are excluded and must be insured in the specialist aviation market.

t: A professional indemnity policy for architects and consulting engineers covers:
o: Cost of rectifying construction defects caused by the contractor
Collapse of a building due to poor workmanship by the builder
Claims arising from the insured's negligent design, specification or supervision causing loss or injury
The insured's loss of fees on a cancelled project
e: The professional's exposure is negligent design or advice; the contractor's workmanship is insured under the contractor's own policies.

topic: Employers' Liability and Employees' Compensation Insurance
t: An employee who is covered under the Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 suffering an employment injury:
o: Cannot claim compensation under the Employees' Compensation Act for the same injury, by virtue of Section 53 of the ESI Act
Can claim only under the EC Act
e: The ESI scheme provides the benefit, and Section 53 bars the employee from recovering compensation or damages from the employer for the same injury.

t: 'Insured persons' under a D&O policy typically include:
o: Past, present and future directors and officers, and often employees acting in a managerial or supervisory capacity
e: Cover follows the individual's capacity as director or officer; auditors and shareholders are potential claimants, not insureds.

t: Which of the following is EXCLUDED under Coverage C (Medical Payments) of the CGL policy?
o: A visitor injured in the insured's office
A customer injured by a falling shelf in the insured's shop
A member of the public injured on the insured's premises
Injury to the insured's own employees arising out of their employment
e: Medical payments exclude employees (workers' compensation territory), the insured's tenants, and injuries within the products-completed operations hazard.

topic: Cyber and Other Specialised Liability Covers
t: 'Notification costs' under a cyber policy are:
o: Costs of informing affected individuals and providing credit monitoring after a data breach
Loss of income following an outage
e: Breach response costs — notification, call centres, credit monitoring — are first-party expenses, often the largest element of a breach.

t: An Insurance Ombudsman can entertain a complaint where the value of the claim, including expenses, does not exceed:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The limit was raised to ₹50 lakh by the amended Insurance Ombudsman Rules.

topic: Underwriting and Claims in Liability Insurance
t: On receiving a third-party claim, the insured under a liability policy must:
o: Admit liability to the claimant promptly
Negotiate and settle the claim directly
Refrain from admitting liability, notify the insurer immediately and co-operate in the defence
Ignore the claim until a court summons arrives
e: Admission or settlement without consent breaches the policy conditions and can prejudice the insurer's defence; control of the claim rests with the insurer.

t: A surplus treaty is one under which:
o: Losses above a retention are paid by the reinsurer
The cedant retains a 'line' and cedes multiples of that line up to the treaty capacity
The annual loss ratio is protected
A fixed percentage of every risk is ceded
e: Surplus is proportional but the ceded share varies by risk size, allowing full retention of small risks; it is used less for liability because 'sum insured' is only a limit.

t: Which of the following cannot be insured under any liability policy?
o: Fines and penalties for criminal offences
Defence costs incurred with the insurer's consent
e: Insuring criminal penalties would be against public policy; liability policies pay civil damages and associated costs only.

topic: Law of Torts and Legal Liability
t: The Fatal Accidents Act, 1855 confers:
o: Compensation on the employee under statute
A right of action on the dependants of a person killed by a wrongful act, neglect or default
e: At common law a death gave no cause of action; the 1855 Act lets the spouse, parent and children sue the tortfeasor for their loss.

t: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 was enacted mainly in response to:
o: The oleum gas leak in Delhi
e: The Act, passed in 1986, gave the Central Government wide powers to regulate hazardous substances after Bhopal; the oleum leak (1985) led to the absolute liability ruling.

t: Legal costs and expenses incurred by the insured in defending a third-party claim, with the insurer's written consent, are under an Indian public liability policy:
o: Payable by the insurer within the limit of indemnity
e: Defence costs are reimbursed but form part of the AOA/AOY limits (costs inclusive); criminal defence costs are a separate extension.

t: A products liability policy is rated at ₹0.50 per mille of turnover. The insured's annual turnover is ₹200 crore. The basic premium is:

A chartered accountant gives incorrect tax advice, and the client is required to pay ₹8 lakh in additional tax and interest. The client sues the CA. Under the CA's professional indemnity policy this claim is:
o: Not covered, since the client's loss is in the nature of tax
Covered, as it is the client's financial loss caused by the insured's negligent professional advice
Covered only if the CA is prosecuted
Not covered, since PI excludes pure economic loss
e: Pure financial loss to a client from negligent advice is precisely what PI insures; only fines on the insured himself would be excluded.

t: The 'allocation' clause in a D&O policy deals with:
o: Allocation of the premium among directors
Apportioning loss between covered and non-covered parties or matters when a claim involves both
Allocation of the limit by territory
e: When a suit names the company (not covered) and its directors (covered), or mixes covered and excluded allegations, the clause fixes how loss and costs are shared.

t: The claims-made version of the CGL form differs from the occurrence version in that it:
o: Contains a retroactive date and provisions for an extended reporting period
Is triggered by the occurrence date
e: The claims-made form was introduced in 1986 to control long-tail exposure; the retroactive date and ERP are its distinguishing features.

t: The IRDAI portal through which a policyholder can escalate an unresolved grievance against an insurer is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Bima Bharosa (formerly IGMS) is the grievance portal; Bima Sugam is the marketplace, Bima Vahak the women-led distribution channel and Bima Vistaar the combined rural product.

topic: Cyber and Other Specialised Liability Covers
t: 'Media liability' in a cyber policy covers:
o: Liability for defamation, infringement of intellectual property or invasion of privacy through the insured's online content
e: Website, social media and digital advertising content create third-party exposure similar to 'personal and advertising injury'.

topic: Cyber and Other Specialised Liability Covers
t: A carriers' legal liability policy generally EXCLUDES:
o: Loss of goods by fire during transit
Damage to goods in a collision
Loss caused by delay, inherent vice, improper packing, and loss of cash or valuables
Theft of goods from the vehicle
e: The policy covers the carrier's legal liability for physical loss from transit accidents; delay and inherent vice are not insurable transit perils and valuables are excluded.

topic: Underwriting and Claims in Liability Insurance
t: A 'hold harmless' clause in a commercial contract is:
o: A contractual assumption of another party's liability, which liability policies generally exclude unless it is an 'insured contract' or specifically endorsed
e: Underwriters review contracts because such indemnities can transfer liability the insured would not otherwise have; the contractual liability exclusion addresses this.

t: Reinsurers favour claims-made wordings for liability business because they:
o: Reduce IBNR uncertainty by limiting the period within which claims can be reported
e: With a claims-made trigger, the exposure of a treaty year is largely known at expiry, improving reserving and pricing.

t: 'Punitive' or 'exemplary' damages are:
o: Awarded to compensate the plaintiff for actual loss
Awarded to punish the defendant for egregious conduct, and are generally excluded from liability policies
Nominal sums awarded when no loss is proved
e: Punitive damages go beyond compensation; most Indian liability policies exclude them, and in many jurisdictions insuring them is against public policy.
